content.comment_body: Hello! I've created several simple projects using [product_name] devices and [product_name] controllers. Each HMI uses buttons to trigger digital outputs. Occasionally, I encounter issues where a network input on the controller doesn't activate when I press a button. In other projects, the input remains activated after downloading and starting the controller. Why does this happen? These are straightforward projects with only about 6–8 buttons on each HMI. I don't have the project file on this computer and can't upload it now, but does anyone have advice or suggestions? [user_name]
Could this be related to a poor network connection? Did you see any error message on the HMI?
No, the HMI doesn’t show any errors. Also, sometimes the input remains active when the device powers on, and I’m unsure why that happens.
It's difficult to provide feedback without reviewing the actual program files.
Hi, is the S7-connection feature enabled on your [product_name] controller? By default, S7 and Modbus connections are disabled in [product_name] controllers running [version_no].
Is the connection only enabled intermittently?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members describe unreliable behavior when using an HMI device to trigger digital outputs on networked [product_name] controllers. Inputs sometimes fail to respond to button presses or remain activated after restarting the controller. These issues persist across different projects, with no error messages displayed on the HMI. Suggested causes include inconsistent network connectivity, specific configuration settings, and default communication protocols.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects dependable operation of the input signals when using HMI buttons, with automatic reset upon reprogramming or power cycling. They are looking for error-free use and predictable controller responses.
